$description: Durations and easings. Every value is one the components already used before it was a token: the eight durations are the enter/leave pairs written into their x-transition attributes, grouped by what moves. Named for the job, like radius, so a new overlay picks the pair for its kind of surface rather than a number. Leave is always quicker than enter: the reader asked for the thing to go, and is already looking at what is next.

duration.$description: Larger surfaces travel further and get longer. Every one of these is a ceiling for something the reader is waiting on, so none goes past 300ms.

enter.$description: A tooltip. Fast enough that hovering along a toolbar does not feel like it lags behind the pointer.
Dropdown, select, combobox and date picker panels: small, and anchored to the control that opened them.
The modal and its backdrop, and the accordion's expand: a surface that changes what the page is about.
Drawer and sheet: a full-height or full-width panel travelling in from an edge, the furthest anything moves.

ease.$description: Two curves, one per direction, and both are the values of Tailwind's own ease-out and ease-in, which is what every component used. Named enter/leave rather than reusing out/in: an @theme key overwrites Tailwind's, and the job is the thing a component author needs to pick by.

enter.$description: Decelerates: arrives quickly and settles, so the surface is readable early.

leave.$description: Accelerates away: the start of the movement is the part the reader sees.
